evidence: The frozen workbook row 41 requires binary pass/fail behaviors and anchored Likert craft. Its internal E42 note discouraging Likert is explicitly superseded for this profile by the frozen skill Known false positives and quality-checks.md:168-170. Parsed all five judge files: 2 gate criteria, 80 Functional criteria and 6 Polish criteria are binary; all 6 Visual criteria are likert with points=5. Every Visual description contains distinct anchors 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 (visual/judge.toml:25-29,40-44,55-59,70-74,85-89,100-104), and visual/prompt.md:45-50 requires integer 1-5 scores and permits full credit without aesthetic perfection. Functional exact outcomes such as restore fidelity and one winner in racing saves are appropriately yes/no (functional/judge.toml:521-525,556-560). Polish checks assess reachability, labels, focus, navigation and recognisable surfaces, not degree of craft (polish/judge.toml:23,32,41,50,59,68); the workspace-organisation threshold permits labels OR layout and does not require aesthetic refinement. Counterexample analysis: a otherwise working app with several distracting font inconsistencies should receive a middle typography anchor, not binary full credit; an app with an inaccessible mobile console fails the concrete responsive usability condition even if attractive. A conforming alternative using native controls, a restrained palette, drawer library and stacked mobile panes can earn full credit under polish:23 and visual:40,55,70,85,99-100. No scale-mismatch false pass or false fail was found. Raw-index hashes all match, but its scripted product observations and screenshots are not configured-judge Likert scores; this Pass is source-based scale-fit review only, not empirical scoring, ranking or runtime clearance.
